meta.scope: Mexico batch 4 — International agreement (T-MEC), education statistics, health/medical (ENSANUT + satellite account + household health spending), public services / governmental quality (ENCIG). Continues push toward broad coverage under the new broader node definition.
meta.target_note: Part of the expansion toward 150+ Mexico candidates. Further batches will continue industrial surveys, more satellite accounts, social programmes/transfers, state-level detail, and additional international links.

candidates.title: Tratado entre México, Estados Unidos y Canadá (T-MEC) / United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA / CUSMA)
candidates.publisher: Gobierno de México / Governments of Mexico, United States and Canada
candidates.description: Trilateral trade agreement that replaced NAFTA and entered into force 1 July 2020. Governs preferential trade, rules of origin (especially automotive), labour, environment, digital trade and other disciplines among Mexico, the United States and Canada. Static legal instrument with no independent statistical publication cadence of its own, but continuously cited in trade statistics, Banxico analysis, and compliance monitoring.
referenced_by: Banxico quarterly reports and special boxes on T-MEC utilisation rates for Mexican exports to the US
Merchandise trade statistics and analysis of preferential vs non-preferential flows
Automotive and manufacturing export compliance statistics
Policy and competitiveness analyses that treat T-MEC rules of origin as the binding institutional framework
candidates.notes:
Prime example of the new rule: a static international treaty that is load-bearing for trade and industrial statistics and is cited on a recurring basis.

Contextual material from Banxico analysis (utilisation of T-MEC for exports to the United States):
Analyses repeatedly report the share of Mexican exports to the US that claim T-MEC preferential treatment (rising sharply in 2025 in response to higher non-USMCA tariffs). Example framing: nearly 100% of certain trucks, ~80% of cars and more than half of auto parts exported by Mexico to the US utilised the T-MEC in recent periods; overall utilisation of the Treaty for Mexican goods entering the US moved from roughly half to well above 75–80% of trade value as tariff differentials increased.

The agreement itself is the permanent legal framework; the statistical system measures compliance with and utilisation of its rules of origin and other disciplines. No separate ‘T-MEC statistical yearbook’ is required for the instrument to qualify — the recurring citation in trade and monetary-policy analysis is sufficient under the expanded node definition.

candidates.title: Estadística Educativa del Sistema Educativo Nacional (Formato 911 / SIGED) / National Education Statistics
candidates.publisher: Secretaría de Educación Pública (SEP) — Dirección General de Planeación, Programación y Estadística Educativa
candidates.description: Official continuous education statistics of the National Education System. Captured each school year via Formato 911 through the Sistema de Información y Gestión Educativa (SIGED). Covers enrolment (alumnos), teachers (docentes) and schools (escuelas) by level, modality, sustained public/private, and entity. Principal indicators (coverage, net enrolment rates, terminal efficiency, dropout, etc.) are published nationally and by state.
candidates.notes: Core education statistical system. SEP integrates the data; INEGI also disseminates related tabulations. Publications such as ‘Estadística e indicadores educativos por entidad federativa’ (cycle 2024-2025 and earlier) provide the official national and state figures. Historical series extend back many decades. This is the primary recurrent source for education counts and indicators used in planning and evaluation.

candidates.title: Censo de Escuelas, Maestros y Alumnos de Educación Básica y Especial (CEMABE) / Census of Schools, Teachers and Students of Basic and Special Education
candidates.description: One-time (2013) comprehensive census of basic and special education schools, teachers and students, ordered as part of the 2012–13 education reform to create a reliable Sistema de Información y Gestión Educativa. Provides detailed infrastructure, staffing and student data that continuous Formato 911 statistics build upon.
referenced_by: Subsequent education planning and SIGED development
SEP statistical publications that still reference the 2013 census baseline for infrastructure and staffing
candidates.notes: Static foundational census for the modern education information system. Even though conducted once, it remains the reference point for the continuous education statistics architecture and is cited when describing the origin of the current SIGED / Formato 911 system. Qualifies under the expanded rule via recurring institutional citation.

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Salud y Nutrición (ENSANUT / Ensanut Continua) / National Health and Nutrition Survey
candidates.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Salud Pública (INSP) / Secretaría de Salud
candidates.description: Flagship health and nutrition survey. Originally periodic; now run as Ensanut Continua with annual fieldwork to support more timely and eventually state-level estimates. Covers health status, nutrition, service utilisation, vaccination, risk factors, and specialised modules (e.g. mental health, lead exposure, cardiovascular). Results used for public-health policy and as a complement to administrative health data.
candidates.notes: Primary population health survey. 2026 wave planned for ~12 000 households with expanded modules. Provides the main survey-based picture of health-service use (public vs private), out-of-pocket burden context, and nutritional status. Complements the administrative and satellite-account health statistics.

candidates.title: Cuenta Satélite del Sector Salud de México (CSSSM) / Satellite Account of the Health Sector of Mexico
candidates.description: Satellite account that measures the economic size of the health sector within the SCNM framework. Reports health-sector GDP, employment, and the contribution of household spending and unpaid health-related work. Consistent with national-accounts concepts and updated annually.
candidates.notes: Key link between health and the national accounts. 2024 results (published 2025): health-sector GDP ~1.75 trillion pesos (5.2% of total GDP); ~2.2 million paid jobs; household contributions (direct spending + unpaid work) exceeding 1.1 trillion pesos. Provides the macroeconomic counterpart to the survey and administrative health data.

candidates.title: ENIGH — Gasto de los hogares en cuidados de la salud / Household health expenditure (from ENIGH)
candidates.description: Component of the Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares that measures out-of-pocket health spending by households. Used to track catastrophic health expenditure, impoverishment due to health costs, and the distribution of the health-financing burden.
candidates.notes: Critical for ‘medical transfers’ and financial-protection analysis. 2024 ENIGH results show average quarterly household health spending rising in real terms; analyses (México Evalúa, CIEP) document increases in catastrophic health expenditure and the regressive burden on lower-income deciles. Complements the CSSSM (which also records household health spending) and ENSANUT (service utilisation).

candidates.title: Encuesta Nacional de Calidad e Impacto Gubernamental (ENCIG) / National Survey of Governmental Quality and Impact
candidates.description: Survey of the population aged 18+ in cities of 100 000+ inhabitants on experiences and perceptions of public procedures and services provided by different levels of government (including security and justice). Measures satisfaction with basic public services (water, sewage, street lighting, garbage collection, police, roads, parks, etc.) and on-demand services, as well as corruption incidence and institutional trust.
candidates.notes: Primary instrument for public-service quality and user experience at municipal and higher levels. 2025 results: overall satisfaction with basic and on-demand public services 47.2%; detailed satisfaction rates for garbage collection (71.5%), drinking water (51.4%), drainage (43.4%), street lighting (41.1%), police (27.9%), etc. Also captures corruption experience and perception. Directly relevant to municipal and state service delivery evaluation.

proposed_edges.basis: Trade statistics and Banxico analysis routinely measure the share of merchandise trade that utilises T-MEC preferential treatment and rules of origin; the Treaty is the institutional framework that defines preferential eligibility.
Satellite account is constructed within the conceptual framework of the Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales de México.
Health-expenditure module is an integral component of the ENIGH questionnaire and results.
The 2013 CEMABE provided the foundational census baseline for the modern Sistema de Información y Gestión Educativa and continuous Formato 911 statistics.
